messages:
martin.ae: Heads-up — Curium Health (regional medtech) asked for a POC with Dedicated capacity and a 40% concession on list for 3 months. They want guaranteed <100ms p50 and SOC2 evidence. Can deal-desk weigh in?
anya.se: thanks — spent an hour with their infra lead. POC is ~200k tokens/month estimate, small model family (open-llama variant). Dedicated pool required to hit latency SLO. Security asks: SOC2 report + IP whitelisting + data-in-transit KMS. They also asked about on-prem later.
julia.deal-desk: 40% is pretty large. Need: 1) current list pricing + target price after concession 2) ask duration, 3) conversion signal (commit or purchase order) 4) any legal holdbacks. Can you post a quick calc?
martin.ae: quick calc below (list = hosted/DC-equivalent pricing for dedicated):
```
List monthly committed cost (dedicated baseline): $25,000
Requested concession: 40% -> $15,000
POC ask (3 months): $45,000 total
Estimated bill to us (infra+ops): ~$18k/mo after GPU allocation -> tight margin
```
carla.finance: margin wise that's rough. If we do 40% without conversion commitment we lose ~$9k/mo. What's the path to revenue?
martin.ae: their CEO said if POC shows 95% latency improvement we get a 12–24mo commit for dedicated. They're comfortable with a 6mo minimum after POC but won't sign without trial results.
ram.legal: any unusual T&Cs? Procurement flagged a 90-day payment term and broad indemnities. We'll need to carve those. Also SOC2 attestation is standard; we can provide, but on-prem ask needs an enterprise SOW.
anya.se: technical blocker: their traffic pattern is bursty, so autoscaling + burst credits needed. That increases infra cost if we commit reserved capacity. Could mitigate with a canary route and overflow to hosted (higher per-token) during spikes — acceptable fallback?
julia.deal-desk: proposal options:
- Option A: Approve up to 30% concession for 3-month POC, conditional on PO for 6mo convertible commit at end of POC, SOC2 provided, 60-day payment max.
- Option B: Approve 40% concession but require 3-month POC fee paid up-front and a non-refundable $15k activation + legal signoff on limited indemnity + conversion LOI within 30 days.
Which do you prefer?
martin.ae: the customer balked at up-front non-refundable. Option A will probably get the POC signed. If we push Option B we risk losing pipeline.
carla.finance: if Option A, add a margin protection: we can cap cumulative concession dollars to $50k and require a minimum committed monthly spend if converted. Also require that any overflow to hosted is billed at full rate (no concession).
sre-bot: Security review flagged missing items: evidence for SOC2 type II or planned audit date, confirmation of KMS integration, IP allowlist IP ranges. Ticket #SEC-3112 created.
ram.legal: I'll draft a short SOW addendum allowing POC on dedicated with limited liability, 60 day payment, and conversion terms. Will need contact from their procurement.
julia.deal-desk: Approval path: deal-desk ok to approve Option A with finance guardrails (cap concession and conversion minimum). Need final confirmation from Martin by EOD + procurement contact.
martin.ae: confirmed — go with Option A + cap $50k + conversion min of $10k/mo for 6 months on conversion. Procurement contact: emily@curiumhealth.com. I'll loop in procurement now.
anya.se: I'll update runbook for burst routing and add fallback to hosted tiers.
carla.finance: ok, Finance signs off on those terms; escalate if they ask to change payment terms.
julia.deal-desk: moving to approve. tagging @ram.legal to review final SOW before signature. :white_check_mark:
ram.legal: will review SOW draft once Martin posts emily contact and PO language.
martin.ae: posted contact and asked for draft SOW — sending to customer now. Thanks all. :pray:
